items.question: What is a kitchen-sink prompt?

options.A: A prompt that contains no few-shot examples
options.B: A prompt focused on a single, well-defined task
options.C: A prompt overloaded with multiple distinct tasks, requirements, and instructions simultaneously
options.D: A prompt that uses all five building blocks in every statement

items.question: What is the 'buried ask' anti-pattern in prompt design?

options.A: Placing the most important instruction in the middle or end of a long prompt where it may receive insufficient weight
options.B: Asking Claude to suppress its reasoning from the output
options.C: Requesting information that Claude cannot retrieve from training data
options.D: Padding the start of a prompt with redundant context to increase its length

items.question: What does an output format specification in a prompt govern?

options.A: The factual accuracy of Claude's claims
options.B: The tone and register Claude uses throughout the response
options.C: The internal reasoning process Claude applies before generating
options.D: The structure, visual presentation, and length conventions of the output

items.question: What makes a prompt exhibit the 'conflicting instructions' anti-pattern?

options.A: Including both a format block and a constraints block in the same prompt
options.B: Including two instructions that cannot both be satisfied simultaneously
options.C: Using both positive and negative framing in the same constraints block
options.D: Providing more than three few-shot examples in the prompt

items.question: What does 'positive framing' mean as a prompting strategy?

options.A: Using encouraging language in the prompt to improve output quality
options.B: Praising Claude's prior response before requesting a revision
options.C: Specifying what Claude should do rather than what it should avoid
options.D: Including only factually accurate background in the context block

items.question: What is the primary cost of 'politeness padding' in a prompt?

options.A: It adds tokens without improving output quality, consuming context window space unnecessarily
options.B: It confuses Claude about which portion of the prompt is the actual task instruction
options.C: It triggers more cautious and hedged responses by signalling uncertainty
options.D: It increases latency because Claude must parse non-instructional content

items.question: What is an iterative refinement loop in the context of prompting?

options.A: A chain-of-thought technique where Claude reasons recursively until it converges on an answer
options.B: A multi-turn conversation strategy that never resets context
options.C: The process of adding more examples to a prompt after each unsatisfactory response
options.D: Using Claude's output as input to a revised follow-up prompt to progressively improve quality

items.question: What is prefilling in Claude prompting?

options.A: Adding background context to the system prompt before the first user turn
options.B: Providing the opening characters or words of Claude's response to steer its continuation from the first token
options.C: Pre-loading reference documents into the conversation context before asking a question
options.D: Setting a few-shot example as the first exchange in every conversation

items.question: What does length and depth control in a prompt govern?

options.A: The number of reference sources Claude will consult when forming its answer
options.B: How many reasoning steps Claude will perform before outputting a conclusion
options.C: Word count targets, level of detail, and the degree of elaboration in the output
options.D: The reading level of the prompt itself

items.question: What is multi-turn conversation management in the context of prompting?

options.A: Structuring exchanges across multiple turns to maintain context, avoid drift, and preserve the relevance of earlier instructions
options.B: Distributing a single task across multiple simultaneous Claude conversations
options.C: Managing the number of few-shot examples added across a conversation's history
options.D: Switching between model tiers across turns to balance cost and quality

items.question: What precisely distinguishes prefilling from a continuation instruction in a prompt?

options.A: Prefilling requires a prior system prompt; a continuation instruction does not
options.B: Prefilling applies only to structured JSON outputs; continuation instructions apply to prose
options.C: A continuation instruction uses positive framing; prefilling uses negative framing
options.D: Prefilling places text inside the assistant turn before generation; a continuation instruction directs Claude to follow from a stated starting point within a normal user or system turn

items.question: When is a negative constraint preferable to positive framing for specifying output behaviour?

options.A: When the desired behaviour is easy to describe in words
options.B: When a specific, well-defined content category must be excluded regardless of how the task is framed
options.C: When the model is already producing output close to the desired style
options.D: When the prompt already contains more than two positive framing directives

items.question: What is the critical structural difference between a kitchen-sink prompt and one with conflicting instructions?

options.A: Kitchen-sink prompts are longer; conflicting-instruction prompts are always short
options.B: Kitchen-sink prompts use negative framing; conflicting-instruction prompts use positive framing
options.C: A kitchen-sink prompt attempts too many tasks simultaneously; conflicting instructions are contradictory and cannot all be satisfied even in isolation
options.D: Kitchen-sink prompts produce no output; conflicting-instruction prompts always produce partial output

items.question: When is starting a fresh conversation the correct choice over continuing to iterate on an existing one?

options.A: When conversation drift has made the thread so noisy that a well-crafted initial prompt would be more reliable than further iteration
options.B: When the user wants to switch to a different model tier for the next response
options.C: When the prior response was completely correct but needs minor formatting changes
options.D: When the task requires fewer than three follow-up turns to complete

items.question: What is the primary advantage of a reusable prompt template with variables over writing a new prompt from scratch for each use?

options.A: Templates prevent Claude from producing inconsistent results across different model tiers
options.B: Templates eliminate the need for context and format blocks in each prompt
options.C: Templates enable few-shot learning without requiring explicit examples
options.D: Templates preserve proven prompt logic and structure while allowing instance-specific values to be substituted efficiently

items.question: What do variables in a reusable prompt template enable?

options.A: Dynamic switching between model tiers based on the variable value
options.B: Substituting instance-specific values while preserving the proven prompt structure
options.C: Attaching different reference documents to each output section automatically
options.D: Adjusting the reasoning depth of the model based on the complexity of the input

items.question: Which TWO behaviours are characteristic of a kitchen-sink prompt? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Bundling multiple distinct tasks into a single prompt that should be addressed separately
options.B: Providing too many few-shot examples for a simple classification task
options.C: Including instructions of unequal priority without signalling which matters most
options.D: Using both positive and negative framing in the same prompt
options.E: Specifying the output format before stating the task

items.question: Which TWO accurately describe prefilling as a Claude prompting technique? (Choose TWO)

options.A: It adds contextual background to the beginning of the user message
options.B: It provides the opening text of the assistant's response before the model generates
options.C: It is equivalent to placing a few-shot example at the very end of the prompt
options.D: It can enforce a specific output format from the first generated character
options.E: It requires the system prompt to define what Claude should continue from

items.question: Which TWO correctly describe effective iterative refinement as a prompting practice? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Each iteration uses the prior output as context and targets one specific remaining gap
options.B: Iterative refinement is always preferable to starting a fresh conversation
options.C: It is most productive when the first output is partially correct and a targeted correction can close the gap
options.D: Each iteration should change multiple variables simultaneously to find the fix as quickly as possible
options.E: Iterative refinement is equivalent to task decomposition since both involve multiple prompting steps

items.question: Which TWO anti-patterns most directly reduce the usefulness of a prompt's first-pass output? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Using XML-style tags for section separation
options.B: Burying the primary task instruction at the end of a long context block
options.C: Stating a word count ceiling in the format block
options.D: Including instructions that contradict each other within the same prompt
options.E: Providing both a role block and a context block in the same prompt

items.question: What is the primary purpose of specifying a word count in the format block?

options.A: To prevent Claude from generating hallucinated content
options.B: To constrain the output to a size appropriate for its intended use context
options.C: To trigger a chain-of-thought reasoning mode for longer responses
options.D: To specify the number of examples Claude should include in its response

items.question: What does a variable in a prompt template represent?

options.A: A model-tier selection flag that routes the prompt to the appropriate model
options.B: A fallback instruction that activates when the primary task cannot be completed
options.C: A chain-of-thought step that the model should elaborate upon
options.D: A placeholder for instance-specific content that changes between uses of the template

items.question: Which building block most directly governs structural presentation conventions such as the use of headings and tables?

options.A: Format
options.B: Constraints
options.C: Role
options.D: Context

items.question: When conversation context has drifted significantly after many turns, what is the most reliable corrective action?

options.A: Add more few-shot examples to the next prompt to reanchor the pattern
options.B: Ask Claude to summarise the entire conversation history before continuing
options.C: Start a fresh conversation with a well-crafted initial prompt that incorporates lessons learned
options.D: Escalate to a more powerful model tier to handle the accumulated context

items.question: From a prompt design perspective, what is the most likely cause when the same prompt produces significantly different outputs across repeated runs?

options.A: The model tier is insufficient for the task complexity
options.B: The prompt is underspecified, leaving too much interpretive latitude for the model to fill
options.C: The output format block has not been declared
options.D: The context block is missing from the prompt

items.question: When is asking Claude to critique its own output most productively used?

options.A: As a complete substitute for human review on consequential outputs
options.B: To reduce the token cost of a second verification pass
options.C: Whenever the first output appears correct but the user wants confirmation
options.D: To surface potential gaps, oversights, or inconsistencies before finalising a draft

items.question: What does the 'change one variable at a time' principle govern in prompt iteration?

options.A: Isolating which specific change caused an improvement or regression, enabling reliable debugging of the prompt
options.B: Limiting the number of building blocks that can be modified between prompt versions
options.C: Ensuring each iteration adds exactly one new constraint to the prompt
options.D: Preventing few-shot examples and chain-of-thought from appearing in the same prompt

items.question: When few-shot examples and chain-of-thought are combined in a single prompt, what does each technique contribute?

options.A: Few-shot increases output length; chain-of-thought reduces it to meet a word count target
options.B: Few-shot selects the model tier; chain-of-thought selects the output format
options.C: Few-shot calibrates the output pattern; chain-of-thought improves reasoning accuracy within that pattern
options.D: Few-shot adds domain knowledge; chain-of-thought provides factual grounding for claims

items.question: What does providing a closing delimiter after reference material in a prompt accomplish?

options.A: It causes Claude to automatically summarise the reference material before proceeding
options.B: It signals clearly where the reference material ends so the model distinguishes it from instructions that follow
options.C: It compresses the reference material to reduce token consumption
options.D: It activates XML-parsing mode for the content that preceded the delimiter

items.question: How does audience calibration differ from tone specification in prompt design?

options.A: They are synonymous — both describe the same thing in the context block
options.B: Audience calibration belongs in role; tone specification belongs in format
options.C: Tone specification is a constraint that prohibits specific styles; audience calibration is a task directive
options.D: Audience calibration describes who the reader is, a situational fact; tone specification describes how the output should sound, a format or role directive

items.question: In a prompt that includes both a role block and a context block, what does the context block add that role alone cannot provide?

options.A: Situational facts about the external world — the audience, prior decisions, and domain background — that shape what a correct answer looks like
options.B: An escalation to a more expert version of the role that the role block alone cannot reach
options.C: A verification mechanism that checks the claims made in the role statement
options.D: Output format constraints that the specified role would conventionally apply

items.question: What risk does prefilling introduce that a standard format instruction does not?

options.A: It prevents Claude from applying chain-of-thought reasoning in the response
options.B: It locks the model into a fixed model tier for the duration of the turn
options.C: If the prefilled text contains an error, the model will continue from it and may propagate the error into the full response
options.D: It prevents the model from accessing content in the system prompt during generation

items.question: What most directly degrades when a single prompt attempts multiple distinct jobs simultaneously?

options.A: The model's access to its training knowledge for each individual job
options.B: The quality and completeness of each job's output due to divided instruction attention and implicit trade-offs
options.C: The accuracy of the format block's directives across the multiple tasks
options.D: The consistency of the role block's influence across the different tasks

items.question: Why does positive framing produce more reliable output behaviour than negative framing when specifying a desired quality?

options.A: Positive framing reduces the total prompt token count
options.B: Positive framing is processed before negative framing in the model's attention mechanism
options.C: Positive framing prevents refusals more reliably than negative constraint instructions
options.D: Positive framing specifies the target precisely, while negative framing eliminates one option without identifying the desired replacement from the remaining alternatives

items.question: When should a practitioner choose a fresh conversation over continued iterative refinement?

options.A: When accumulated context drift or compounding errors make a well-crafted new initial prompt more likely to succeed than further iteration on the current thread
options.B: When the prior response was close to correct but needed a small formatting change
options.C: When the task requires more than five follow-up prompts to complete
options.D: When the model has produced a response that matches the format block exactly but is factually wrong

items.question: What does adding a format block to an existing prompt that lacks one primarily fix?

options.A: Wrong factual content in the output
options.B: Missing domain knowledge in the response
options.C: Output that is structurally unusable for its intended purpose despite being factually correct
options.D: Insufficient reasoning depth on a complex analytical task

items.question: Which TWO are legitimate and beneficial uses of reusable prompt templates? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Automatically generating few-shot examples for each new task instance
options.B: Standardising prompt structure across a team so all members use proven prompt logic
options.C: Eliminating the need for the task block in high-frequency routine prompts
options.D: Replacing reference material with variable placeholders that the model fills from training knowledge
options.E: Reducing per-use prompt writing effort for recurring tasks with varying inputs

items.question: Which TWO are accurate statements about effective iterative refinement? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Targeting one specific gap per iteration prevents corrections from disrupting already-correct elements
options.B: The more iterations performed, the closer the final output will inevitably be to the ideal
options.C: The prior output should be provided as context for each follow-up refinement prompt
options.D: Every task benefits from at least three iterations before being considered complete
options.E: Iterative refinement is interchangeable with task decomposition for multi-step tasks

items.question: Which TWO statements correctly characterise the relationship between positive framing and negative constraints? (Choose TWO)

options.A: They cannot coexist in a well-designed prompt
options.B: Positive framing specifies desired behaviour; negative constraints exclude specific content categories
options.C: Negative constraints are more reliable than positive framing for all instruction types
options.D: Both can appear in the same prompt, serving complementary and non-conflicting functions
options.E: Positive framing belongs in the task block; negative constraints belong in the role block

items.question: Which TWO correctly identify when chain-of-thought is more appropriate than few-shot examples as the primary technique? (Choose TWO)

options.A: When the task requires sequential logical reasoning where errors in intermediate steps would compound
options.B: When the output format is difficult to specify in words
options.C: When the primary failure mode is logically inconsistent or incorrect reasoning rather than wrong output format
options.D: When the task involves matching a specific brand voice or style that must be consistent
options.E: When the number of available worked examples is fewer than three

items.question: Who is the primary intended user of the Claude API, compared with the Claude.ai chat interface?

options.A: Developers and technical teams building applications or automated workflows
options.B: Business professionals who need faster response times than the chat interface provides
options.C: Enterprise users who have exceeded the message limits of their chat subscription
options.D: Teams that need to persist more documents than a Project knowledge base allows

items.question: When Claude's output quality is unsatisfactory, which approach should a team exhaust first?

options.A: Fine-tune the model on domain-specific examples
options.B: Improve the prompt with clearer instructions and representative examples
options.C: Switch to a higher-tier model for deeper reasoning capability
options.D: Reduce input length to remove noise from the context

items.question: Why must an API key never be placed in a shared document or team messaging channel?

options.A: The key expires automatically once copied into a non-technical document
options.B: Anyone who reads the document gains the ability to make billable API calls on the account's behalf
options.C: Shared keys trigger an automatic compliance flag that suspends the associated account
options.D: Claude.ai blocks API requests from keys that have appeared in plaintext communication logs

items.question: Which statement BEST describes how API usage cost accumulates across a single request?

options.A: Cost is based solely on output tokens; input is treated as a query fee covered by the plan tier
options.B: Cost is a flat rate per API call, independent of message length or content
options.C: Cost accrues on output tokens only; longer inputs reduce cost by shortening required output
options.D: Both the tokens sent to the model and the tokens the model generates contribute to the billable total

items.question: Claude stops generating a response mid-way through a lengthy task, even though the input supplied was small. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The model paused to await confirmation because output exceeded a safety-review threshold
options.B: The context window filled due to previous conversation turns consuming available space
options.C: The response reached the model's maximum output length, a constraint separate from the context window
options.D: The rate limit was reached mid-response and generation was suspended

items.question: Which situation MOST clearly indicates a team's workflow has outgrown Claude.ai chat and requires API access?

options.A: The team wants to format responses as polished Artifacts rather than plain chat text
options.B: Team members are sharing a Project with colleagues in other departments
options.C: Claude must be embedded in the team's internal ticketing system to process requests programmatically
options.D: Prompt length has grown too long to type comfortably in a single chat message

items.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of the system prompt in an API integration?

options.A: To inject the model's internal training guidelines into each conversation at runtime
options.B: To allow the application developer to set persistent instructions that apply to every user interaction before the end user speaks
options.C: To supply a cache of recent conversation history so the model can reference prior sessions
options.D: To configure the model tier selection and token budget for each API call

items.question: What is the PRIMARY advantage of retrieval-augmented generation over placing an entire document corpus in the context window on every call?

options.A: Retrieval produces higher answer accuracy because the model analyses every document fully
options.B: Retrieval guarantees factual responses by blocking the model from using parametric memory
options.C: Retrieval removes the need for a vector database by encoding documents in the model weights
options.D: Retrieval reduces cost and latency by fetching only relevant document fragments rather than processing the full corpus each time

items.question: Which characteristic BEST distinguishes an agentic workflow from a single-shot prompt?

options.A: Agentic workflows are restricted to predefined task sequences approved by a developer in advance
options.B: An agentic workflow always produces a longer final output than a single-shot prompt
options.C: Agentic workflows require a larger model tier and cannot run on smaller, faster models
options.D: An agentic workflow enables the model to call tools, evaluate intermediate results, and decide subsequent steps across multiple turns

items.question: Batch processing via the API is MOST appropriate for which type of workload?

options.A: High-volume, non-time-sensitive tasks where results can be delivered within hours rather than seconds
options.B: Interactive applications where a user expects a response while they wait on-screen
options.C: Sequential workflows where each task depends on the output of the previous before it can proceed
options.D: Exploratory prompt iteration where a practitioner is refining a prompt in real time
